newsitem.title: GERMANY: KfW paid 2.1 bln dmk for Lufthansa stake.
newsitem.headline: KfW paid 2.1 bln dmk for Lufthansa stake.

text.p: Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW), the state-owned German development agency, said on Thursday it paid 2.1 billion marks ($1.3 billion) for taking over the state's 36 percent stake in airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG in December.

KfW took over the stake as a prelude to full privatisation of Lufthansa and will act as a temporary trustee for the stake until it is sold to the private sector at the end of 1997, KfW chief executive Gert Vogt told a news conference.
Vogt said KfW had financed the 2.1 billion-mark payment by issuing bonds.
KfW currently holds 38 percent of Lufthansa's capital.
Vogt said such transactions were not unusual for KfW and that it had played a similar role in the privatisation of industrial conglomerate VIAG.
